A planet’s bulk density depends not only on its composition but also on how strongly its own gravity compresses it.  

• Planet a: Same mass and radius as Earth ⇒ same density as Earth ≈ 5.5 g cm⁻³.  
• Planet b: Explicitly given density ≈ 5.5 g cm⁻³ (same as Earth).  
• Planet c: Same composition as Earth but 5 M⊕. Greater gravity compresses the interior, so its radius grows by less than a factor of (5)¹ᐟ³; the result is a higher mean density than Earth (≈ 6–7 g cm⁻³).  
• Planet d: Same composition but 0.5 M⊕. Weaker self-gravity → less compression → radius decreases by less than (0.5)¹ᐟ³, so its density is lower than Earth’s.

Therefore, planet c has the highest density.

Option mapping:
(A) corresponds to c.

Answer: A
